articles.title: Six wins, one terrible loss: Mt. Silver turns to Crem
articles.dek: Josh Alakazam is out for the season. Crem Ftzpatrik delivered three touchdowns in relief as the Reds beat Cianwood 27–7.
articles.author: ellis-quill

body.text: Mt. Silver won comfortably and left with the kind of news that makes a final score feel briefly unimportant. Josh Alakazam is out for the season. The Reds are 6–0, their defense has allowed 45 points, and the quarterback who helped put them there now carries a 16-week absence on the injury report. A week after losing Garshawn Lynch, Connor McLarren has another central piece to replace.

Crem Ftzpatrik gave him a useful place to start. The Alcremie completed 15 of 18 passes for 135 yards and two touchdowns, added a one-yard rushing score, and helped finish a 27–7 win at Cianwood. There was an interception and there were three sacks. There was also a team continuing to function after an afternoon changed beneath it. Both parts belong in the account.
I'd rather Josh were answering these questions. I'm glad we got the win. The receivers made it much easier to say the calls out loud and get on with them.
body.speaker: Crem Ftzpatrik

body.text: Alakazam had been perfect through the air: seven attempts, seven completions, 56 yards. His final passing line includes a four-yard touchdown to Vibrava on fourth-and-three with 2:03 left in the first quarter. That aggressive finish gave Mt. Silver a 7–0 lead. The game report does not identify the precise injury play, and there is no reason to attach the injury to that touchdown merely because it was the most memorable thing he did.

What the record does show is the transfer of responsibility. In the second quarter, with 2:21 remaining, Ftzpatrik threw short right to Ariados for a 14-yard touchdown. The Reds led 14–0. A Stunky recovery of Bibarel's fumble earlier in the quarter had given the defense its own contribution to the change in momentum. Cianwood was being asked to catch up against a team that could still complete ordinary passes.
The receivers made room

Plusico Buress caught all eight of his targets for 54 yards. Tony Gyarzalez caught all six of his for 50. Those are strikingly unglamorous totals beside such clean catch counts, and that is why they matter. The Reds had two dependable destinations helping turn available throws into finished plays. Ftzpatrik did not have to throw for 300 yards to keep his first extended assignment moving.

Buress also had something of his own to answer. His late fumble was part of the danger in the previous week's 24–20 escape at Oreburgh. This time the Reds lost no fumbles. He did not score, but he did complete every catch the offense asked of him. A receiver can make a quarterback feel less alone without producing a spectacular play.
Throw it to me. That's what I wanted him to hear. I can't fix what happened to Josh, and I can't replay last week. I can catch the next one.
body.speaker: Plusico Buress

body.text: The running game helped, too. Raticate carried ten times for 66 yards, while Vibrava added 27 on seven attempts. Mt. Silver finished with 103 rushing yards on 22 carries. With Lynch still facing five more weeks out, those supporting contributions will become a regular subject rather than a footnote. The Reds have now had to redistribute both the throws and the handoffs.

Cianwood did make the substitute uncomfortable. Beedrill sacked Ftzpatrik twice and Victreebel once. Golbat intercepted a deep-left throw with 38 seconds left before halftime. That sequence is a fair warning against treating a successful relief appearance as an instant solution to every future problem. There will be throws to reconsider and protection work to do before Petalburg arrives.

The defense kept those mistakes affordable. Cianwood managed 183 total yards, converted three of eleven third downs, and did not score until 1:23 remained in the fourth quarter. Gardevoir's late eight-yard touchdown to Doduo reduced the margin after the Reds had already built a 27–0 lead. The Crushers fell to 2–4; a competitive stretch of their season has become an increasingly expensive collection of losses.
An unbeaten team with a new assignment

Ftzpatrik's one-yard run on third-and-one, with 48 seconds left in the third quarter, made it 20–0 before the missed extra point. In the fourth, Machamp intercepted Gardevoir, and Ftzpatrik later found Raticate for an eight-yard score to the right. The relief quarterback's touchdowns came through two different receivers and his own short run. The ball still had several ways to reach the end zone.

McLarren's immediate task is to preserve that breadth. Petalburg is 5–1 and has just held Mauville to nine points. The next opponent will have a full week to consider the quarterback it is likely to face. A successful afternoon against Cianwood gives the Reds evidence that they can compete with Ftzpatrik. It does not give them permission to ask him to become Alakazam by the next kickoff.

There is a particular cruelty in the timing. Last week's headline said the next six weeks had become harder. Now the change reaches beyond the halfback position and beyond that period. Mt. Silver still owns every win it earned, still leads its conference's playoff order, and still has a defense capable of making a modest offensive day sufficient. Those advantages are real, and they are worth protecting while the offense learns a different rhythm.

Ftzpatrik does not have to make the whole season understandable at once. His first answer was a short-right touchdown to Ariados. His last was another to Raticate. Between them, the Reds found enough football to get to six wins.

art.alt: Silver and red quarterback helmets numbered 7 and 12 beside a football.

articles.title: Ninety-four yards. Then ninety-four more.
articles.dek: My Way, Son returned two kickoffs for touchdowns, ran for 118 yards and helped Rustboro turn Dewford's big plays into a 37–21 defeat.
articles.author: calvin-rook

body.text: Dewford scored the sort of touchdown that should change a game: a 96-yard interception return by Gligar with one second left in the first quarter. Rustboro answered on the next kickoff. Then Dewford scored again in the second quarter, and Rustboro answered on that kickoff, too. Both returns traveled 94 yards. Both belonged to My Way, Son. The Breakers kept finding the end zone and then losing the benefit before their defense could get comfortable.

Rustboro won 37–21 behind an Iron Treads performance that makes a normal all-purpose line look insufficient. My Way, Son ran eighteen times for 118 yards, caught two passes for 45, and returned three kicks for 226 with two touchdowns. Add those yards and you get 389. The total includes returns, of course, but Dewford still had to defend every one of them.
The second one still needed the blocks. I know people will see the two numbers and talk about me. I saw the lanes, and I tried to stay patient long enough to use them.
body.speaker: My Way, Son

body.text: Tyler Scarboro's club needed a result with some force behind it. A week earlier, Rustboro lost 12–10 to Pewter despite Philly's 97 rushing yards. Four field goals beat an offense that had done enough between the lines and too little with its chances. This time the Stone scored 24 points in the second quarter alone. The final whistle brought them to 3–3 and pushed them into sixth place in the Hoenn–Sinnoh playoff order.
Dewford could not keep a lead

The opening was hardly tidy. Shieldon lost a fumble after a short-right completion in the first quarter, and Frosmoth then threw the interception that Gligar took almost the entire length of the field. Rustboro had given away two possessions before it had scored. The seven-point deficit at the quarter break was small compared with how damaging the sequence could have felt.

Numel's kickoff opened the second quarter. My Way, Son took it 94 yards for a touchdown, and Gorebyss's extra point tied the game. At 3:08, Dewford's Frosmoth threw deep left to Watchog for a 41-yard score. Numel converted, kicked off, and watched the same Iron Treads go the same distance again. The score was tied at fourteen after a second return that was every bit as costly as the first.

There is no useful way to soften that for Brawly. Two scoring plays had created two opportunities to defend a lead. Neither opportunity survived the kickoff. Dewford could still make a spectacular play, but its coverage unit kept requiring another one. A team already missing Excadrill and Ambipom did not need to keep restarting its offensive work from a level score.

Rustboro finally moved ahead through its passing game. Frosmoth found Gengar deep right for an eighteen-yard touchdown with 1:03 left in the half. Gorebyss added a 43-yard field goal with twelve seconds remaining. A quarter that began with the Stone trailing 7–0 ended with them leading 24–14. The return touchdowns changed the pace, and the offense used the extra breathing room.

Gengar's appearance also belongs to this week's story. The former Haunter is now back with Rustboro after the trade-related evolution, and the recorded scoring play names Gengar. There is no need to turn the sequence into a new destination or a permanent departure. The relevant sight for Dewford was a receiver in Rustboro's offense finishing an eighteen-yard touchdown.
The ground game stayed on the field

The Stone did not spend the second half waiting for another return. They finished with 222 rushing yards on 37 carries. Philly contributed eighty yards and a touchdown on twelve attempts, while My Way, Son supplied the larger share. Rustboro converted seven of ten third downs. Dewford converted none of six. That difference kept one offense working and sent the other looking for another sudden answer.

Armaldo recovered two Dewford fumbles in the third quarter, one after a completion to Boldore and another after an Unfezant run. Frosmoth scored on a three-yard run with 2:13 left in that quarter. In the fourth, Milotic intercepted a deep-right pass and returned it 26 yards. Philly's three-yard touchdown at 3:48 pushed the lead to 37–14 before the missed extra point.
Ninety-four twice is showing off. I had three yards to get and got them. They all go on the same scoreboard, so I'm happy to let him do the long commute.
body.speaker: Philly

body.text: Dewford's late two-yard touchdown run by Pidgeotto made the final margin sixteen. The Breakers still finished with only seven first downs against Rustboro's twenty-two, and their 219 total yards were well behind the Stone's 365. The return story is enormous, but it should not conceal how much ordinary possession football Rustboro won after the early mistakes.

There was a substantial cost on defense. Parasect is listed out for five weeks after this game. That matters for a team trying to turn a .500 record into sustained progress rather than another weekly reversal. Azalea is next, fresh from a second consecutive win. Rustboro cannot assume that a pair of kickoff touchdowns will travel with it.

For Dewford, now also 3–3, the trip to Olivine carries a more immediate question. The Breakers have lost a game in which they produced a 96-yard defensive touchdown and a 41-yard passing score. The repair starts with the moments after they score. Twice against Rustboro, the celebration lasted only as long as Numel's kickoff.

art.alt: My Way, Son, Iron Treads No. 93, carrying a football in Rustboro brown and silver.

articles.title: Four touchdowns, no punts: Ninjaskamara keeps Mossdeep rolling
articles.dek: A 213-yard day from scrimmage and a suffocating run defense carried the Eclipse past Lavaridge, 41–3, to 6–0.
articles.author: mara-voss

body.text: The most revealing eight seconds of Mossdeep's 41–3 win came just before halftime. With 37 seconds left, Lavaridge faced fourth-and-two and Delphox was sacked by DurrickBurgess. With 29 seconds left, Dram Marino threw deep left to Ninjaskamara for a forty-yard touchdown. A possible Inferno drive became seven Eclipse points almost immediately. Mossdeep's offense did not need to be asked twice.

Ninjaskamara finished with four touchdowns: three rushing and one receiving. His twelve carries produced exactly one hundred yards; his four catches produced 113 more. The Eclipse improved to 6–0, stretched their season scoring margin to plus-201, and gave Lavaridge a second straight week without a touchdown. The final was comprehensive even though the opening quarter had ended tied at three.

On the pass, I wanted to secure it before I thought about the finish. You get a chance like that after the defense makes a play, you don't want to give the chance back. The run scores were the same idea: find what is there, keep the ball safe.
body.speaker: Ninjaskamara

body.text: Marino completed nineteen of 33 passes for 262 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions. He was not sacked. Mossdeep did not punt. The offense produced twenty first downs and 456 total yards, with 194 coming on the ground. There were incomplete throws and early drives that ended in field goals, but the Eclipse kept enough possessions alive to make those imperfections relatively inexpensive.

Adam Vinathorn opened the scoring with a 55-yard field goal at 4:30 in the first quarter. Lavaridge answered through Charjabug from fifty yards with 1:47 left. That was the last time the Inferno scored. Vinathorn's 25-yard kick early in the second put Mossdeep back ahead, and Ninjaskamara's three-yard run up the middle at 2:55 supplied the first touchdown.
The halfback was not alone

Marshall Flock had the same number of carries as Ninjaskamara and gained 77 yards. After last week's two-return-touchdown feature, Flock's contribution was quieter and thoroughly useful. Mossdeep could keep handing the ball off without asking one runner to supply every yard. Ninjulio Jones added nineteen yards on two rushes, while Marino's two kneels accounted for the small subtraction at the bottom of the team total.

Gronkaludon caught four passes for 57 yards. Ninjulio caught four for 33. Travis Meltce added 23 on two catches, and both Lorenzo Steel and Vita Weba contributed fourteen receiving yards. The offense found several short gains around Ninjaskamara's explosive catches. Its longest reception was a 48-yarder by the halfback; the scoring catch before halftime went forty. They were different plays, and Lavaridge had to survive both.

I liked the carries. Last week everybody wanted to talk about the returns, which was nice. This week I got to help keep us moving. If he's finishing the drives, I'm fine being one of the reasons we got there.
body.speaker: Marshall Flock

body.text: The offensive line supplied a particularly clean platform. Gene Shuckshaw and Shuck Bednarik each recorded nine pancakes and a 100 percent block-win figure. Bastony Boseli recorded twelve pancakes. Those numbers do not require the invention of a particular blocking assignment on a particular touchdown. Alongside zero sacks allowed, they describe an afternoon in which the ball carriers and quarterback had considerable help.

The Conkeldurr in the pivotal sack was another change worth recognizing. DurrickBurgess had completed his trade evolution before this game and appeared in the recorded play as Conkeldurr. The defensive box score divides that sack credit, giving him half a sack and Shawn Mareman half. The play log names the finisher; the individual totals preserve the shared credit. Both show a defense ending the possession when Lavaridge needed two yards.
Fifteen rushing yards, zero third-down conversions

Lavaridge's problems began before the passing downs. Swampert managed ten yards on eight carries, with a long gain of ten. The Inferno finished with fifteen rushing yards on eleven attempts. Derrat Brooks recorded ten tackles and four tackles for loss. Mossdeep repeatedly made a small rushing workload produce almost nothing, leaving Delphox to keep finding completions without a dependable second route forward.

Delphox did complete seventeen of 26 passes for 172 yards and threw no interceptions. Staravia caught eight for 63. Those are respectable individual fragments inside a team performance that produced no third-down conversions in seven attempts. Clay Rathews recorded two sacks, and the Inferno lost a fumble after a fourth-quarter completion to Tropius. Luvrelle Revis recovered it. Lavaridge finished with eight first downs.

Ninjaskamara's six-yard run to the right with 2:55 left in the third quarter made it 27–3 after the extra point. His nine-yard run up the middle at the start of the fourth supplied his fourth touchdown of the day. Poury Holt later caught an eight-yard pass to the left on third-and-three for the final touchdown. The Eclipse kept scoring without needing a return or interception touchdown to enlarge the margin.

Lavaridge fell to 2–4 and now travels to Blackthorn. Mantine is listed out for two weeks after the loss, adding a secondary problem to a difficult stretch. Mossdeep goes to Lavender, which had a bye and remains 4–1. That will ask a different question of Michael Dorrill's team than two consecutive home wins by a combined ninety points to six.

The Eclipse can take this much with them: no punts, no sacks allowed, no turnovers, and four touchdowns from a halfback who required only sixteen touches from scrimmage. Lavender has a week of rest. It will need a plan for number twenty-seven.

art.alt: Ninjaskamara, Ninjask No. 27, carrying a football in Mossdeep magenta and gold.

articles.title: Venomoth finds 69 yards of breathing room
articles.dek: Saffron survived Fuchsia 16–14 after a late deep strike, five sacks and a final possession that never went back to the Shadows.
articles.author: rowan-vale

body.text: Saffron spent most of this game looking like a team that had misplaced its comfortable win. Then Venomoth found it, sixty-nine yards down the right side. Archiekazam's touchdown pass with 3:44 left in the fourth quarter gave the Psi Corps just enough room to survive Fuchsia 16–14. The room was promptly reduced, but it was never completely taken away.

The result leaves Saffron 5–1 and Fuchsia 0–6. The experience was much closer than those records suggest. The Shadows outgained the Psi Corps 270–267, collected thirteen first downs to ten, and converted six of fourteen third downs. Saffron converted none of four. If you arrived expecting another version of last week's 48–0 win over Lavaridge, you were following the wrong script by the fourth quarter.
The score made that throw important, but I wanted the read to stay the same. We had the chance to the right. Venomoth finished it. After that, the job was getting the next possession right, too.
body.speaker: Archiekazam

body.text: Archiekazam completed eleven of fifteen passes for 174 yards and two touchdowns without an interception. Venomoth caught both of his targets for 98 yards. HeeDee Lamb caught all four of his for 39 and the other touchdown. There was efficiency when Saffron actually threw, but the offense did not get enough sustained work to make its early lead comfortable.

Lamb's nine-yard touchdown catch to the left, with 2:51 remaining in the first quarter, opened the scoring. Gorebyss added a 44-yard field goal early in the second. At 10–0, Saffron had the lead, the pass rush and the reputation. It did not have an afternoon that could be safely filed away. Vigoroth's second-quarter fumble, recovered by Cacturne, was one reason the distance stayed manageable.
The sacks bought time

Fuchsia's Empoleon completed 25 of thirty throws for 204 yards and two touchdowns. That completion rate makes the five sacks stand out even more. Saffron did not spend the day intercepting him; neither quarterback threw a pick. The defense instead took yards and possessions away before the completed passes could become enough points.

Watchog supplied a first-quarter sack on third-and-three. Verrick Brooks, the Victreebel wearing number 52, added two sacks in the first half. Pawmo got another on third-and-eight before the break. Kecleon brought Empoleon down on third-and-nine in the third quarter. Those five plays cost Fuchsia 33 yards, and three of the sacks explicitly came on third down. The pressure was doing work the final two-point margin can obscure.

The Shadows kept coming anyway. Oinkologne ran thirteen times for 58 yards and caught four passes for 27. Heatmor had 49 receiving yards, Gumshoos 37, and a broad collection of short targets kept Empoleon's completion total climbing. Fuchsia did not need one receiver to overpower the game. It needed enough of those completed throws to become scores before the clock disappeared.

The first touchdown finally arrived with 4:09 left, when Empoleon threw short right to Palpitoad for six yards on third-and-four. The extra point made it 10–7. Saffron answered within the next minute: Archiekazam threw deep right to Venomoth on second-and-nine, and the receiver went 69 yards for the touchdown that restored a nine-point lead. Gorebyss missed the extra point, so nine was all the cushion Saffron had.
I was glad the ball came my way. He gave me a good throw, and I wanted to finish it for him. We still had work after the score. Nobody on their side had decided to stop.
body.speaker: Venomoth

body.text: Fourteen points were real pressure

Fuchsia's second touchdown came on fourth-and-seven. Empoleon found Weepinbell short right for thirteen yards with 2:09 remaining, and Clamperl's extra point cut it to 16–14. It was an impressive conversion under a demand that could not be postponed. The Shadows had turned a game with almost three scoreless quarters into a finish where one more possession might matter.

They did not get that possession. At the two-minute warning, Saffron had second-and-one. Watchog ran right for five, then up the middle for seven. Archiekazam completed a fourteen-yard pass to Watchog on second-and-three. The quarterback could then kneel twice. The final stretch was a sequence of practical gains by the same player who had helped start the pass rush much earlier.

Gorebyss finished one-for-two on field goals and one-for-two on extra points. Fuchsia missed its only field-goal attempt. Those lost points belong in the explanation, but neither side can solve the game by casually adding its misses to the score. Saffron still had to earn the final first downs. Fuchsia still had to reach those fourth-quarter touchdown chances after absorbing five sacks.

Trent Scarboro also takes an injury concern into the bye: Vigoroth is listed out for three weeks. He had carried ten times for 73 yards, a productive line alongside the lost fumble. His absence changes the distribution of useful rushing work, and the bye gives Saffron time to consider it. Fuchsia hosts Veilstone next while still missing Sharpedo, listed out four weeks.

For the Psi Corps, this was a win worth keeping and a performance worth correcting. For the Shadows, it was their strongest argument in a while that the next close finish need not end like the others. The difference this time was sixty-nine yards to Venomoth, followed by three gains from Watchog that kept the ball away.

art.alt: Venomoth No. 88 carrying a football in Saffron pink and pale blue.

articles.title: Sunyshore gets its returns the right way round
articles.dek: Pat Serptain's 63-yard punt touchdown and Fred Whirler's late pick-six powered a 34–7 response to last week's loss.
articles.author: tessa-wren

body.text: Sunyshore had spent a week on the wrong side of a return story. Against Veilstone, the Starseekers wrote two of their own. Pat Serptain took a punt 63 yards for a touchdown early in the third quarter. Fred Whirler returned an interception thirteen yards for another late in the fourth. A 34–7 win moved Sunyshore to 5–1 and gave Karson Jones something considerably more pleasant to discuss than Milotic's previous visit.

The defense made the response convincing. Veilstone gained 115 total yards, managed five first downs and converted one of thirteen third downs. Tatsugiri threw two interceptions and was sacked four times. The Fists had one scoring drive, following their own interception, and very little sustained offense around it. Sunyshore did not need its attack to be flawless to take control.

That distinction matters because the Starseekers did punt five times. DeZhaun Watzon threw an interception, and the offense converted only three of nine third downs. The final margin should not be mistaken for an afternoon of uninterrupted offensive efficiency. Sunyshore won with a passing game that finished chances, a return game that supplied a touchdown, and a defense that kept creating another opportunity.

A punt is a very polite invitation to borrow the football. I thought sixty-three yards was a reasonable borrowing distance. The blockers might ask for their share of the credit, and they would be right.
body.speaker: Pat Serptain

body.text: The first fourteen came through the air

Watzon completed nineteen of 31 passes for 162 yards and three touchdowns. The first two went to the receiver recorded as Buizel in the game, who has since evolved into Floatzel. The identity is the same player; the game-day catches happened as Buizel. He finished with six receptions for 55 yards and two scores, a compact line with a substantial effect on the scoreboard.

The opening touchdown was a seven-yard pass deep left with 3:18 left in the first quarter. The second was a one-yard pass short left with 31 seconds remaining in the half. Duosion made both extra points, and Sunyshore led 14–0 at the break. The offense had not run away in yardage, but it had converted two possessions into the largest available return.

Myles Gabite carried six times for 38 yards. BAXXED? added fifteen on four attempts, and Scol Alexander contributed six on two. Sunyshore finished with 65 rushing yards on seventeen carries, including Watzon's running and late kneels. Sceptile caught five passes for 46 yards, while Fera LaGatr had four for 34 and the third passing touchdown. The attack had several supporting pieces even with the modest total of 227 yards.

After halftime, the defense quickly returned Veilstone to its punter. Conkeldurr sacked Tatsugiri for seven yards on second-and-ten. At 5:15, Sunflora punted fifty yards to the Sunyshore 37. Serptain took the ball the remaining 63 yards for the touchdown, and the extra point made it 21–0. He finished with six returns for 125 yards. One of them had done most of the damage.

The Fists briefly found a route back when Corviknight intercepted Watzon's deep-left pass and returned it twenty yards. Palpitoad completed the subsequent scoring chance with a five-yard run up the middle late in the third quarter. At 21–7, Veilstone had finally scored and had evidence that the opposing quarterback could give it another opening. The next interception, however, went the other way.
The fourth quarter belonged to the defense

Jolt Vick intercepted Tatsugiri's short-left throw on third-and-eleven with 5:10 remaining and returned it 44 yards. Watzon later found Fera LaGatr short left for a nine-yard touchdown. Duosion missed the extra point, leaving the score 27–7. The interception had supplied the kind of change in field position that made a modest passing total much more effective.

Whirler completed the scoring at 1:46. Facing fourth-and-eleven, Tatsugiri threw short middle and the Poliwrath took the interception thirteen yards into the end zone. Whirler's defensive line included five tackles, two tackles for loss, four pressures and that touchdown. It was an emphatic finish to a day in which Veilstone rarely escaped the next difficult down.
I wanted the ball. Once I had it, I wanted the end zone. We had done too much work putting them in those downs to let the last part of the game get soft.
body.speaker: Fred Whirler

body.text: Torten Carter recorded two sacks, with the other two supplied by Conkeldurr and Dragonair. Veilstone's Whiscash managed thirteen rushing yards on sixteen carries. That combination explains why the Fists kept arriving at situations where a short completion was unlikely to be sufficient. Even their final possession contained two more sacks before a six-yard completion on fourth-and-26 ended it.

The win does not erase last week's 33–20 loss to Violet or answer every question about Sunyshore's consistency. It does show a team capable of directing the next game rather than extending the previous one's frustration. The Starseekers now have a plus-95 scoring margin and sit second in the Hoenn–Sinnoh playoff order. Cerulean, coming off a 20–3 defeat at Vermilion, is next on the road.

Veilstone fell to 3–3 and travels to Fuchsia, where the winless Shadows have just taken Saffron to a two-point finish. That opponent will look at one conversion in thirteen third-down tries and believe there is a game to win. Sunyshore can look at Serptain's punt return and Whirler's interception and enjoy a simpler conclusion: this week, the return touchdowns belonged to them.

art.alt: Pat Serptain, Serperior No. 39, carrying a football in Sunyshore magenta and black.
